chunks: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Ishaq al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Abu Uruba al-Husayn b. Abi Ma'shar al-Harrani and Abu Talib b. Abi Awana informed me. They said: Abu Dawud Sulayman b. Sayf al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Waqid narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz al-Majashun, from Muhammad b. al-Munkadir, from Jabir b. Abdullah. He said:

The angels were made happy on the Day of Badr and Hunayn when Ali (peace be upon him) cleared the brigades from before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). So whoever is not made happy by the sight of Ali (peace be upon him), then the curse of Allah is upon him.

key_terms.اسْتَبْشَرَتِ: Were made happy; the angels expressed joy and gladness
key_terms.الْأَحْزَابَ: The brigades/factions; referring to enemy groups in battle

ai.seo_question: What did Jabir b. Abdullah say about the angels rejoicing for Ali at Badr and Hunayn?
ai.summary: Jabir b. Abdullah, a prominent companion of the Prophet, reports that the angels rejoiced during the battles of Badr and Hunayn when Imam Ali (AS) drove the enemy factions away from the Prophet (SAWW). The hadith emphasizes that anyone who does not feel joy at seeing Ali faces divine curse, underscoring his supreme status among the companions. These were pivotal early Islamic battles where Ali's valor was decisive.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Ishaq al-Dinawri narrated to us. He said: Abu `Uruba al-Husayn b. Abi Mu`shir al-Harrani and Abu Talib b. Abi `Uwana informed me. They said: Abu Dawud Sulayman b. Sayf al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Waqid narrated to us from `Abd al-`Aziz al-Majashun from Muhammad b. al-Munkadir from Jabir b. `Abdullah.  He said:

The angels were made happy on the Day of Badr and Hunayn when `Ali (as) cleared the brigades from before the Messenger of Allah (s). Whoever is not made happy by the sight of `Ali (as), then the curse of Allah is upon him.
